Footer.rights: Lumo TV provides, hosts and resells no content.

Landing.metaTitle: Lumo TV — IPTV player for Android, Android TV and the web
Landing.metaDescription: Lumo TV plays your own M3U playlist or Xtream Codes account on your phone and on your television. No channels included: you bring the source.
Landing.heroSubtitle: Register an M3U playlist or an Xtream Codes account and find your channels, your favourites and your progress on your phone and on your television alike.
Landing.heroNotice: Lumo TV is a player. We provide no channels, no bouquets and no content.
Landing.valueOneBody: Your channels are synchronised once, on the server, then available on each of your devices along with your favourites and your progress.
Landing.valueTwoBody: The Android TV app is driven entirely by the remote control. You activate your television from your phone, so there is no password to type on a D-pad.
Landing.valueThreeBody: Your source credentials are encrypted before they are stored, and are never returned by our API — not even to you.
Landing.howStepOneBody: By email or with Google. The account is what carries your sources across your devices.
Landing.howStepTwoBody: An M3U playlist URL, or the host and credentials of an Xtream Codes account.
Landing.howStepThreeBody: The stream goes straight from your own server to your device. It never travels through our infrastructure.
Landing.guidesTeaserBody: Understand the formats, set up a source, install on a television.

Guides.metaTitle: IPTV guides — M3U playlists, Xtream Codes, Android TV
Guides.metaDescription: Practical, provider-neutral guides: the difference between M3U and Xtream Codes, setting up a playlist, playback on Android TV.
Guides.indexIntro: General explanations of the formats and the settings. No provider is named, recommended or supplied.

m3u-playlist.title: Setting up an M3U playlist
m3u-playlist.description: What an M3U file is, what it carries, and how to register it in a player.
m3u-playlist.intro: An M3U playlist is a plain text file listing streams. It is the most widespread format, and the poorest: it carries neither a structured catalogue nor account information.
m3u-playlist.sectionOneBody: Each entry starts with an #EXTINF line that may carry attributes: tvg-id to join the channel to the programme guide, tvg-logo for its logo, group-title for its category. A channel with no group-title lands in an "Uncategorised" group.
m3u-playlist.sectionTwoBody: A URL is preferable: it re-synchronises on its own when your provider adds or removes channels. An imported file is frozen at the moment of import.
m3u-playlist.sectionThreeBody: M3U carries no EPG. You supply the URL of an XMLTV file separately — often compressed — which the player normalises on its side.

xtream-codes.title: M3U or Xtream Codes: what is the difference
xtream-codes.description: How the two ways of reaching a source compare, and why one gives a far better experience than the other.
xtream-codes.intro: Both lead to the same streams. What changes is everything the player can show around them.
xtream-codes.sectionOneBody: An API returns a structured catalogue: live channels, films, series, categories, the programme guide and account information — including the expiry date and how many simultaneous streams are allowed. An M3U returns a flat list.
xtream-codes.sectionTwoBody: A host, a username and a password. The host is accepted with or without a scheme, with or without a port, with or without a trailing slash: normalisation happens on the server.
xtream-codes.sectionThreeBody: It is encrypted before it is written to the database, with a key that is not in that database. It is returned by no API response, and appears in no log.

android-tv.title: Watching IPTV on Android TV
android-tv.description: What changes between a phone and a television, and how to pair the two without typing a password on a remote.
android-tv.intro: A television is not a large phone: it is driven by a remote, from three metres away, and typing on it is punishing.
android-tv.sectionOneBody: The television shows an eight-character code. You open the activation page on your phone, already signed in, and enter that code. The television signs itself in within seconds.
android-tv.sectionTwoBody: Every selectable element has to be unmistakable: the focused one grows, takes a border and lifts off the background. Nothing may be reachable by pointer only.
android-tv.sectionThreeBody: Many televisions crop the edges of the picture. A five per cent margin is reserved on each side so that nothing important falls outside the visible area.
